title: Connectivity-Aware Exploration of Robotic Grasp Spaces
abstract: arXiv:2609.22983v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robotic grasping is typically formulated as the problem of identifying successful actions from a space of candidate grasp poses. However, the organization of successful actions within this space has received less attention. We study the multiscale structure of viable robotic grasps in $SE(3)$ and investigate whether this structure can be exploited for more efficient exploration. Using a large-scale grasp dataset, we show that successful grasp sets exhibit heterogeneous and reproducible connectivity structure across objects. We then introduce a connectivity-aware sampling strategy that incrementally explores the currently observed grasp space by prioritizing potential bridges between components, structural frontiers, boundary extensions, and geometric novelty. translated_title: 连接性感知的机器人抓取空间探索
translated_abstract: 机器人抓取通常被表述为从候选抓取位姿空间中识别成功动作的问题。然而，成功动作在该空间中的组织方式却较少受到关注。我们研究了SE(3)中可行机器人抓取的多尺度结构，并探讨这种结构是否可以被利用来实现更高效的探索。利用大规模抓取数据集，我们证明了成功抓取集合在不同物体之间表现出异构且可复现的连接性结构。随后，我们提出了一种连接性感知的采样策略，通过优先考虑组件之间的潜在桥梁、结构前沿、边界扩展和几何新颖性，逐步探索当前观测到的抓取空间。在受控重建实验中，该方法恢复成功抓取集合连接性结构的效率显著高于随机采样和最远点采样。
tldr: 该论文发现机器人成功抓取集合在SE(3)空间中具有异构且可复现的连接性结构，并提出一种连接性感知的采样策略，能够比随机采样更高效地重建和探索抓取空间的结构。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that successful robotic grasp sets exhibit heterogeneous and reproducible connectivity structure in SE(3), and proposes a connectivity-aware sampling strategy that reconstructs and explores grasp space structure far more efficiently than random sampling.
